 JUDGMENT

This suit is filed by the plaintiffs against the defendant - B.D.A. for the relief of permanent injunction with respect to suit property more specifically described in the plaint schedule and for costs of the suit.

The case of the plaintiff in brief is as under: -
Originally the land bearing Sy.No. 223/1 of Kodihalli Village measuring 27 guntas out of 34 guntas of land was granted by the Deputy Tahasildar under Inam Abolition Act in favour of original propositus Pichchanna S/o. Kuppanna @ Munishyamappa on 4.12.1958.
The said Munishyamappa executed Will dated 1.6.1971 in favour of his daughter-in-law Smt.Munichinnamma W/o.Shyamanna.
The partition was taken place between Smt.Munichinnamma and her six sons on 6.8.2011.
By virtue of the said partition, the suit property is fallen to the share of plaintiffs - husband and wife.
Plaintiffs came into possession and enjoyment of the suit property as owners and possessors.
Their names are entered in BBMP records, they are paying tax to BBMP.

It is further case of the plaintiffs that,
defendant without having right, title or interest, tried to interfere the possession of the plaintiffs over the suit property and hence, cause of action arose to the plaintiffs to file this suit.
So, plaintiffs prayed to grant the decree of permanent injunction as against the defendant not to interfere the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the plaintiffs over the suit property.

sentences.text: On service of suit summons, defendant - B.D.A. appeared and filed written statement.
In its written statement defendant has denied the ownership and possession of the plaintiffs over the suit property.
It has denied that suit property is fallen to the share of plaintiffs by virtue of registered partition deed.
contended that the statutory notice under Section 64 of B.D.A. Act is not issued to the defendant and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

It has also contended that Sy.No.223/1 measuring 34 guntas of Kodihalli Village was standing in the name of one Kuppanna @ Muniswamy and the said land was acquired by BDA under preliminary notification dated 28.11.1959.
Final notification was made on 19.8.1964.

The said land was acquired to form a layout "Between Old Madras Road and HAL Road II Stage"
by paying compensation to the owner Kuppanna.
So, plaintiffs are the land grabbers and unauthorised occupants having no manner of right, title or interest over the Sy.No. 223/1.
The suit property described in the plaint does not exist at all.

It is also contended that by suppressing the real facts, plaintiffs have filed this false / 6 /
O.S.No.4530/2021 suit and there is no cause of action to file the suit.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the suit with costs.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
(1) Whether the plaintiffs prove that they are in possession and enjoyment of suit schedule property as on the date of suit ? (2) Whether the plaintiffs proves the interference of the defendant ? (3) Whether the defendant proves that the Civil Court has no jurisdiction U/Sec.6 of Land Acquisition Act ?
(4) What order or decree?
6.
In order to prove the case, the plaintiff No.1 has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to P.16.

In order to rebut the case of the plaintiffs, the / 7 / O.S.No.4530/2021 A.E.E. of B.D.A. got examined himself as D.W.1 and got marked Ex.D.1 to 3.
7.
Heard both sides.
Perused the pleadings, issues, oral and documentary evidence and materials on record.

8. My findings to the aforesaid Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the negative Issue No.2 : In the negative.
Issue No.3 : In the affirmative.

sentences.text: REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.3 : - The burden of proving this issue is upon the defendant.

It is specific case of the defendant that, Sy.No. 223/1 was acquired long back and compensation was paid to the owners and now the / 8 / O.S.No.4530/2021 plaintiffs cannot claim possession over the suit property.
They have also contended that suit itself is not maintainable before the Civil Court.

In order to prove that suit property was acquired by B.D.A., defendant has relied upon Ex.D.1 to D.3 Ex.D.1 is the preliminary notification passed by the Government dated 28.11.1959, which discloses that Sy.No.223/1 Kodihalli Village was proposed for acquisition and preliminary notification was published in Mysore Gazette.
It also discloses that the said property was measuring 34 guntas and was standing in the name of Kuppanna and Muniswami.

Ex.D.2 is the final notification dated 19.8.1964 published in Mysore Gazette, which also discloses that B.D.A. acquired Sy.No.223/1 measuring 34 guntas which was standing in the name of Kuppanna and Muniswami for formation of / 9 / O.S.No.4530/2021 layout named as 'between Old Madras Road and HAL II Stage'.

Ex.D.3 is the extract of the register maintained by SLAO, which discloses that the compensation was received by A.Shamanna with respect to acquisition of land bearing Sy.No. 223/1 measuring 34 guntas, which discloses that on 21.12.1976 the possession of the land was taken.

In O.S.No.4528/2021 defendant has produced the certified copy of the Judgment passed by the learned IX Additional City Civil And Sessions Judge,
Bengaluru in O.S.No.1332/2003, which discloses that the suit filed by wife and sons of A.Shamanna for the relief of declaration and permanent injunction with respect to the very Sy.No.223/1 of Kodihalli Village was dismissed with costs.

sentences.text: In said suit, the competent Civil Court has held that the plaintiffs have not proved their title and possession over / 10 / O.S.No.4530/2021 the suit property.
In said case it was also held that A.Shamanna has received compensation through cheque.
So, the contention of the plaintiff that this land was never acquired by B.D.A. cannot be accepted.
The said A.Shamanna who received compensation is none other than the husband of Smt.Munichinnamma.
So, after receiving compensation, the family of plaintiffs lost right, title and interest over the suit property.
Plaintiff No.1 is none other than the son of A.Shamanna.
Since the entire survey number was acquired by B.D.A., the question of formation of plots in the said survey number and putting khatha numbers is against the rules and regulations.

10. Defendant has not produced separate documents to show that possession was taken by B.D.A.,
but after passing final notification the award was passed / 11 / O.S.No.4530/2021 by SLAO and award amount was received by the father of plaintiff No.1 i.e., A.Shamanna.
So, without challenging the acquisition proceedings, plaintiffs cannot file suit for bare injunction.

11. On this point there is a direct ruling of the Hon'ble Apex Court filed by the present defendant - BDA reported in (2013) 3 3 Supreme Court Cases 66 - Commissioner, Bangalore Development Authority and another Vs. Brijesh Reddy and another, wherein it is held as under :

servants and anyone claiming through them from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule property.
It is true that there is no challenge to / 12 / O.S.No.4530/2021 the acquisition proceedings.

However, in view Venkatesh S vs The Bangalore Development Authority on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91499639/
4 of the assertion of BDA. in their written statements, about the initiation of acquisition proceedings ending with the passing of award, handing over possession and subsequent action, etc. the said suit is not maintainable.

sentences.text: This was rightly concluded by the trial court.
For proper compensation, the aggrieved parties are free to avail the statutory provisions and approach the court concerned.
All these aspects have been clearly noted by the trial court and ultimately it rightly dismissed the suit as not maintainable.

On the other hand, the learned Single Judge of the High Court though adverted to the principles laid down by this Court with reference to acquisition of land under the Land Acquisition Act and Section 9 CPC, committed an error in remanding the matter to the trial court on the ground that the plaintiffs were not given opportunity to adduce evidence to show that their vendor was in possession which entitles them for grant of permanent injunction from evicting them from the scheduled property without due process of law by the defendants.

In the light of the specific assertion coupled with materials in the written statement about the acquisition of land / 13 / O.S.No.4530/2021 long ago and subsequent events, suit of any nature including bare injunction is not maintainable, hence, we are of the view that the High Court is not right in remitting the matter to the trial court for fresh disposal."

12. In another decision reported in AIR 2019 KARNATAKA 205 - G.V.Reddy Vs. Ministry of Communication Employees Co-Operative Housing Society Ltd., Bangalore the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held as under :
"Civil P.C. (5 of 1908), 0.39 R.1, 0.7 R.11(a), S.9 - Temporary injunction - Jurisdiction of Civil Court - Land in question already acquired by Acquisition Authority before its purchase by plaintiff - Proceedings in respect of land would be governed by Land Acquisition Act which is special and comprehensive Act - Remedy even for relief of injunction is not available before Civil Court - Plaint liable to be rejected.

16. So, the present suit filed by the plaintiffs seeking the relief of injunction against the B.D.A. is not at all maintainable and this Court has no jurisdiction to try and entertain the suit.
As per Section 9 of the C.P.C., this Court cannot decide this suit as the jurisdiction of Civil Court is exclusively barred under Land Acquisition Act.
Hence, I answer Issue No.3 in the affirmative.

/ 16 / O.S.No.4530/2021 17. ISSUE NO.1 : - Plaintiffs have produced photograph, its receipt and CD, khata certificate, tax paid receipts and encumbrance certificate to show their possession over suit property.
But, the entire land measuring 34 guntas in Sy.No.223/1 itself was acquired by B.D.A.
So, the subsequent partition deed dated 6.8.2011 between family members themselves will not create any right, title or interest in favour of the plaintiffs over the acquired land.
It appears that plaintiffs got divided Sy.No.223/1 as Khata No.150, 150/1 to 150/6 and got entered their names in BBMP records.
Giving khata number to survey number itself is illegal.
Defendant in its written statement has contended that plaintiffs are unauthorised occupants over the suit property.

So,
even if plaintiffs are in possession of the suit property, it is not / 17 /
O.S.No.4530/2021 lawful possession.

A.Shamanna after receiving compensation,
cannot continue with possession of the suit property.
The counsel for plaintiffs argued that defendants have not taken possession of the suit property by following due process of law, hence, plaintiffs possession has to be protected.
But, it is not the case of plaintiffs to grant injunction restraining the defendant not to interfere possession of the plaintiffs without due process of law.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Brijmohan Reddy case as stated above are pleased to hold that the Judgment passed by the Hon'ble High Court that plaintiff shall not be dispossessed without due process of law is not proper and correct.
So, the said contention of the plaintiffs cannot be accepted in this case.
However, plaintiffs have sought absolute injunction.

If absolute / 18 / O.S.No.4530/2021 injunction is granted in favour of the plaintiffs,
then plaintiffs may misuse the same and obstruct the defendant from taking due process of law.
So, I hold that plaintiffs have not proved their possession over the suit property as lawful possession.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the negative.
18. ISSUES NO.2 AND 4 : - Plaintiffs have not proved their possession over the suit property.
Hence, the question of interference to their possession does not arise.
